title: Rust: Observable Stream
description: Implement a simple observable stream with push-based notifications.

steps.title: Observable Trait
steps.description: Define a trait `Observable<T>` with `fn subscribe(&mut self, observer: Box<dyn Fn(&T)>)` and `fn unsubscribe(&mut self, id: u64)`. Create a `Subject<T>` that stores observers and notifies them. Test with string values.
hints: `trait Observable<T> { fn subscribe(&mut self, observer: Box<dyn Fn(&T)>); fn unsubscribe(&mut self, id: u64); }`
`struct Subject<T> { observers: Vec<(u64, Box<dyn Fn(&T)>)>, next_id: u64 }`

verification.failureMessage: Create a Subject, subscribe, and push a value.

steps.title: Map Operator
steps.description: Create a `map` function that transforms a stream: `map(stream, |x| x * 2)` returns a new stream. Subscribe to the mapped stream and test with integer values.
hints: Subscribe to the source stream, transform the value, push to the new subject.
`fn map<T, U, F>(source: &mut Subject<T>, f: F) -> Subject<U> where F: Fn(&T) -> U`

verification.failureMessage: Push 1,2,3 through a map(x2) stream and print 2,4,6.

steps.title: Filter Operator
steps.description: Create a `filter` operator: `filter(stream, |x| x > 5)` only pushes values matching the predicate. Push values [1, 7, 2, 9, 3] and print filtered results.
hints: Subscribe to source, check predicate, push to output if true.
`fn filter<T, F>(source: &mut Subject<T>, predicate: F) -> Subject<T> where F: Fn(&T) -> bool`

steps.title: Debounce Operator
steps.description: Implement a `debounce` operator that only emits a value after a period of silence. If a new value arrives within the debounce period, reset the timer. Simulate with timestamps.
hints: Track `last_emit: Instant` in the debounce state.
When a value arrives, check if enough time has passed since last emit.
If not, skip the value (or schedule it).

verification.failureMessage: Push rapid values and show only the last one emits.

steps.title: Rx-Style Chain
steps.description: Chain operators: create a source stream, apply `map(|x| x * 2).filter(|x| x > 10)`, subscribe and print. Push [3, 7, 5, 9] and show the transformed output.
hints: Each operator returns a new Subject that can be further chained.

verification.failureMessage: Chain map then filter and print 14 and 18.
